passages.context: Read in the retrieved transcription with the surrounding account of Nero's chariot-driving in view. Registered as the one well-attested napkin signal of classical antiquity, whose sense is the opposite of the meaning the modern folded-napkin claim assigns to a napkin gesture.

work.author: Suetonius
work.description: Suetonius's lives of the first twelve Caesars, written about 121. The life of Nero records that a freedman dropped the napkin to start the races in the Circus Maximus, which is the one well-attested napkin signal of classical antiquity and means begin, not I am returning. A locus is Life.chapter.section.
work.title: De vita Caesarum
